title: Nucleated polymerization of prion aggregates (Rubenstein et al., 2007)
reference: Rubenstein R, Gray PC, Cleland TJ, Piltch MS, Hlavacek WS, Roberts RM, Ambrosiano J, Kim J-I (2007). Dynamics of the nucleated polymerization model of prion replication. Biophys Chem 125:360-367. doi:10.1016/j.bpc.2006.09.011

lambda__FREE.note: PrPC production, molecules/day; also sets the initial PrPC level x_0 = lambda/d

d__FREE.note: PrPC clearance, /day; also sets the initial PrPC level x_0 = lambda/d

a__FREE.note: degradation or sequestration of a whole aggregate, /day. not identifiable: measured leverage 0 sigma in both directions. Aggregates grow at about beta*x = 22 /day over this window, so clearing whole aggregates at 0.047 /day changes the trajectory by a fraction of a percent. It is identifiable in the published year-long protocol, not in five days. Reported by a fit but never scored.

beta__FREE.note: elongation by conversion of one PrPC at an aggregate's free end, /(molecule*day)

b__FREE.note: cleavage of one inter-subunit bond, /day; with a it sets the steady-state mean chain length a/b + 2n - 1

notes: Aggregate-size dynamics under a stoichiometry-bounded network: 121 species and 3,843 reactions generated from seven rules, with the observables summarizing a chain-length distribution rather than naming individual species. Two features make it unlike the rest of the collection. The PrPSc population grows exponentially across the window, from 9 molecules to tens of thousands, so early and late points differ by three orders of magnitude and the chi-square is dominated by the late ones. And lambda and d set the initial PrPC level as well as its turnover, so they are the only free parameters in the collection that move the initial condition; a fit that gets their ratio right but their scale wrong matches the early data and misses the take-off. The budget is the collection's smallest, 2,000, because a trajectory costs about 0.36 s.
